blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know how a round of Read the Sky plays and how it scores.
Read the Sky is a picture quiz against the clock. It is on Slieve Commedagh, the fourth place on the Summit Ready map.
You build one game from each pair of game chapters. Read the Sky is paired with Route Timer, so you build one of those two.
First you build Read the Sky exactly as it is in Summit Ready. Then, in stage 5, you change it into a timed picture quiz on your own topic.
A round has 10 questions. Each question shows a photo of the sky and asks what it means for a walk in the hills.
There are 3 answers down the right-hand side, and only one of them is right. The [[time bar|0]] above them gives you 10 seconds to pick one.

words: time bar
The green bar on the right of Read the Sky. It starts full and gets shorter until the time is up.
bin\Debug
The folder inside your project where Visual Studio 2019 puts the program it builds. Summit Ready reads its data, pictures and sounds from there.
zip file
One file with other files and folders packed inside it.
property
A named value that an object carries, such as `Question` on a SkyQuestion. `{ get; set; }` lets other code read the value and change it.
constructor
A method with the same name as its class. It runs once, when code makes a new object with `new`.
static
A method marked `static` belongs to the class itself. You call it on the class name, as in `SkyQuestion.LoadAll()`.
List
A list that grows as you add to it. `List<SkyQuestion>` is a list that holds SkyQuestion objects.
continue
Inside a loop, `continue` skips the rest of this turn of the loop. The loop goes straight on to its next turn.
array
A row of values of the same type, kept together under one name and numbered from 0. `answers[0]` is the first answer button, and `answers[2]` is the third.
Convert.ToInt32
Turns text into a whole number. `Convert.ToInt32("2")` gives the number 2.
lightning bolt
The button at the top of the Properties window that shows a control's events in place of its properties.
field
A variable written at the top of the class, outside every method. Every method in the form can use it, and it keeps its value until the window closes.
panel
A control that holds other controls. `pnlPlay` is the play area that holds the photo, the time bar and the answers.
PictureBox
A control that shows a picture. `picSky` shows the photo of the sky.
ProgressBar
A control that shows a bar. `prgTime` is the time bar, and its length is its Value out of its Maximum.
Timer
A control that never shows on the window. Once started, it runs its Tick method every time its Interval runs out, until it is stopped.
Interval
How long a Timer waits before each Tick, in thousandths of a second. 100 means 0.1 seconds.
Tick
The event a Timer has. Its method runs every time the Timer's Interval runs out.
event
Something that happens to a control, such as a click on a button, or a Timer ticking.
handler
The method that runs when an event happens. `Answer_Click` is the handler for a click on any of the 3 answer buttons.
sender
Every handler is given `sender`: the control that the event happened to, such as the answer button that was clicked.
colour from red, green and blue
`Color.FromArgb(62, 142, 65)` mixes a colour from red, green and blue. Each number is from 0 to 255.
Cursor
The mouse pointer's shape over a control. `Cursors.Hand` is a pointing hand, and `Cursors.Default` is the normal arrow.
count up with ++
`++` adds 1 to a whole number. `right++` means right becomes one more than it was.
count down with --
`--` takes 1 away from a whole number. `timeLeft--` means timeLeft becomes one less.
or
`||` means or. The `if` is true when any one of its parts is true.
and
`&&` means and. The `if` is true only when both of its parts are true.
not equal
`!=` means is not equal to. `picked != -1` is true when picked is any number except -1.
Substring
Gives part of some text. `Substring(0, 1)` gives the first letter, and `Substring(1)` gives everything after the first letter.
ToLower
Gives a copy of some text in small letters. `"Hill fog".ToLower()` gives `"hill fog"`.
AddRange
Adds every item of one list to the end of another list in one go.
red underline
The wavy red line Visual Studio 2019 draws under code it does not understand yet. Often it means a method you have not written yet.

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know what each line of `sky.txt` holds.
Read the Sky gets its questions from a text file, `sky.txt`. The file is already in your bin\Debug\Data folder, because `summit-ready-files.zip` put it there in chapter 2.
The file has 12 questions, and each round uses 10 of them in a random order. So no two rounds are the same.
You do not type `sky.txt`. You read it here, so that the code in stage 4 makes sense.

partLines: The first question

Each line is one question, in 8 parts with a bar `|` between them. Part 1, `sky-cumulonimbus.jpg`, is the file name of the photo, in the Images\Sky folder. Part 2, `Thunderstorm cloud`, is a short name for the sky. The feedback at the end of the round uses it. Part 3 is the question. Parts 4, 5 and 6 are the 3 answers. Part 7 is the number of the right answer, 1, 2 or 3. Here it is 1, so `Get off the high ground now` is right. Part 8 is the reason, which shows under the photo after an answer.
The other 11 questions
The other 11 lines have the same 8 parts, in the same order.

box.title: If a file is missing or broken

blocks.p: Read the Sky never crashes because a file is missing. This is what you see instead.
If `sky.txt` is missing, or has fewer than 10 good lines, no question appears. The words above the photo say **Read the Sky needs 10 questions in Data\sky.txt, each with 8 parts.**
If a line of `sky.txt` does not have exactly 8 parts, Read the Sky skips that line.
If a sky photo is missing, that question shows an empty white box in place of the photo.
If a sound is missing, that moment is silent, and the game carries on.
To put a missing file back, you download the [[zip file|2]] again and paste its folders into bin\Debug. When Windows asks about the files you already have, you click **Skip these files**.
Skipping keeps every file you already have, including any file you changed. Only the missing files are copied in.

code.title: SkyQuestion.cs: the SkyQuestion class
code.why: You type the 6 properties, and the 6 lines that put a value into each one, because they are new. The rest reads a file the same way as `LoadAll` in chapter 3, so it comes in the copy.
partLines: The class and its 6 properties

`class SkyQuestion` starts the class. Each property holds one part of a line of `sky.txt`. `Answers` is an array of 3 strings, one for each answer. `Right` is a whole number, so it is an `int`. `{ get; set; }` lets other code read each property and change it.
The constructor

This part is the constructor. It runs when code writes `new SkyQuestion(parts)`. `parts` is one line of `sky.txt`, already cut into 8 pieces at each bar. The first 3 pieces go into `Picture`, `Name` and `Question`.
The 3 answers
`new string[] { parts[3], parts[4], parts[5] }` makes an array from the 3 answers, in the order they are in the file.
The number of the right answer
`parts[6]` is text, such as `"1"`. `Convert.ToInt32` turns it into the number 1. The file counts the answers from 1, but an array counts from 0. So `- 1` turns 1, 2 or 3 into 0, 1 or 2.
The reason
`Explanation` holds the reason that shows under the photo after an answer.
The start of LoadAll

`static` means that you call LoadAll on the class itself, as `SkyQuestion.LoadAll()`. LoadAll starts with an empty list. `Files.Data` from chapter 2 gives the full path of `sky.txt` in the Data folder. If `sky.txt` is not there, LoadAll hands back the empty list, so the game shows a message and does not crash.
Read every line

The StreamReader opens `sky.txt`. The loop goes round once for each line, until the end of the file. `Split('|')` cuts each line at each bar into `parts`. If a line does not have exactly 8 parts, `continue` skips it. Every good line becomes a new SkyQuestion, and `questions.Add` puts it on the end of the list.
Close the file and hand back the list
`reader.Close()` closes `sky.txt`, so that other programs can open it again. `return questions;` hands the full list back to the code that called LoadAll.

code.title: The Read the Sky fields
code.text:
// ---------- Read the Sky ----------
private List<SkyQuestion> questions;   // every question in sky.txt
private int[] order;                   // the questions, mixed up
private int number = 0;                // this question, 0 to 9
private Button[] answers;              // the three answer buttons
private int[] answerOf = new int[3];   // the answer on each button

private int right = 0;                 // right answers so far

private List<string> wrongLines = new List<string>();

`questions` holds every question that LoadAll reads from `sky.txt`. `order` holds the question numbers in a random order. `number` counts the questions in this round, from 0 to 9.
The answer buttons

`answers` is an array that keeps the 3 answer buttons together, so a loop can reach each one. `answerOf` says which of the 3 answers in the file is on each button. `new int[3]` starts all 3 values at 0.
The state of a question
`answered` turns true once the player answers, or the time runs out. `timeLeft` counts tenths of a second, so 100 is 10 seconds. `right` counts the right answers.
The feedback
`wellLines` and `wrongLines` collect the lines for What went well and What went wrong, one line for each question.

blocks.p: The file lists the 3 answers in one order. The buttons show them in a mixed order, so the right answer is not always at the top.
If `answerOf[0]` is 2, the top button shows the third answer in the file.
When the player clicks the top button, the code checks whether `answerOf[0]` is the right answer's number.

code.title: tmrQuestion_Tick and Answer_Click
partLines: One tick less
tmrQuestion_Tick runs every time the Timer ticks. `timeLeft--` takes 1 off `timeLeft`, and the time bar's Value follows it, so the bar gets shorter.
The last 3 seconds
`||` means or. At 3 seconds, 2 seconds and 1 second left, the tick sound plays.
Time is up
When `timeLeft` reaches 0, Answer runs with -1. No button is number -1, so -1 means that no answer was picked.
Only one answer
Answer_Click runs when the player clicks any of the 3 answer buttons. If this question is already answered, `return` stops it, so the click does nothing.
Which button
`sender` is the button that the player clicked. The loop compares it with each answer button in turn. When they match, Answer runs with the button's number, 0, 1 or 2.

glossary: time bar
The green bar on the right of Read the Sky. It starts full and gets shorter until the time is up.
bin\Debug
The folder inside your project where Visual Studio 2019 puts the program it builds. Summit Ready reads its data, pictures and sounds from there.
zip file
One file with other files and folders packed inside it.
property
A named value that an object carries, such as `Question` on a SkyQuestion. `{ get; set; }` lets other code read the value and change it.
constructor
A method with the same name as its class. It runs once, when code makes a new object with `new`.
static
A method marked `static` belongs to the class itself. You call it on the class name, as in `SkyQuestion.LoadAll()`.
List
A list that grows as you add to it. `List<SkyQuestion>` is a list that holds SkyQuestion objects.
continue
Inside a loop, `continue` skips the rest of this turn of the loop. The loop goes straight on to its next turn.
array
A row of values of the same type, kept together under one name and numbered from 0. `answers[0]` is the first answer button, and `answers[2]` is the third.
Convert.ToInt32
Turns text into a whole number. `Convert.ToInt32("2")` gives the number 2.
lightning bolt
The button at the top of the Properties window that shows a control's events in place of its properties.
field
A variable written at the top of the class, outside every method. Every method in the form can use it, and it keeps its value until the window closes.
panel
A control that holds other controls. `pnlPlay` is the play area that holds the photo, the time bar and the answers.
PictureBox
A control that shows a picture. `picSky` shows the photo of the sky.
ProgressBar
A control that shows a bar. `prgTime` is the time bar, and its length is its Value out of its Maximum.
Timer
A control that never shows on the window. Once started, it runs its Tick method every time its Interval runs out, until it is stopped.
Interval
How long a Timer waits before each Tick, in thousandths of a second. 100 means 0.1 seconds.
Tick
The event a Timer has. Its method runs every time the Timer's Interval runs out.
event
Something that happens to a control, such as a click on a button, or a Timer ticking.
handler
The method that runs when an event happens. `Answer_Click` is the handler for a click on any of the 3 answer buttons.
sender
Every handler is given `sender`: the control that the event happened to, such as the answer button that was clicked.
colour from red, green and blue
`Color.FromArgb(62, 142, 65)` mixes a colour from red, green and blue. Each number is from 0 to 255.
Cursor
The mouse pointer's shape over a control. `Cursors.Hand` is a pointing hand, and `Cursors.Default` is the normal arrow.
count up with ++
`++` adds 1 to a whole number. `right++` means right becomes one more than it was.
count down with --
`--` takes 1 away from a whole number. `timeLeft--` means timeLeft becomes one less.
or
`||` means or. The `if` is true when any one of its parts is true.
and
`&&` means and. The `if` is true only when both of its parts are true.
not equal
`!=` means is not equal to. `picked != -1` is true when picked is any number except -1.
Substring
Gives part of some text. `Substring(0, 1)` gives the first letter, and `Substring(1)` gives everything after the first letter.
ToLower
